title: Training Taste — Thais Castello Branco, Taste Labs
talk_summary: A design-quality startup founder argues that AI output 'slop' is measurable via small trained classifiers ('probes') over structured features (color, typography, layout, fit-to-context), which outperformed LLM-as-judge at detecting AI-generated sites. She proposes decomposing fuzzy quality into objective sub-checks, extracting brand/context into structured specs agents can follow, and using these as gates before shipping.

takeaways.technique: Small trained classifiers ('probes') instead of LLM-as-judge for specific defect classes
takeaways.what_they_do: Pattern-mine structured features from a large corpus, train tiny binary classifiers per characteristic, and combine their frequency to predict a quality failure; this beat asking an LLM to judge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This performed better, by the way, than like most LLM as a judge methods of like asking an LLM to like judge if that uh is like great human quality versus like AI-generated slop.
takeaways.numbers: 2M+ websites analyzed; claims 'super high' prediction ability, no precise metric given

takeaways.technique: Decompose fuzzy quality into objective sub-problems before measuring
takeaways.what_they_do: Break a subjective domain into components specific enough to be near-deterministic (contrast, alignment, palette) versus genuinely subjective parts, then measure the objective ones.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're trying to train a model to be good at selecting color palettes or have contrast or alignment, those are things that if you define the problem and the context in a specific enough way

takeaways.technique: Extract fuzzy context (brand/style) into a structured spec the agent follows and you can verify against
takeaways.what_they_do: Take a brand URL, extract into specific structured components an agent can follow, and use the same spec as a verification rubric so you can see where the agent deviates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how do we turn something as fuzzy as a brand into something so structured that it becomes easy to for your agent to follow that but also for you to judge against it

takeaways.what_they_do: Define domain expectations, then intentionally diverge on a few dimensions while adhering to the rest, rather than randomizing via temperature.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's not just about like turning up the temperature of the model and and kind of fingers crossed hoping for the best

takeaways.technique: Quality gate before shipping ('gate for slop')
takeaways.what_they_do: Use the probe/classifier layer as a gate that blocks the agent from shipping low-quality output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how we can actually like use this to be even become a gate for slop and and not let your agent ship slop
